# VIBE CODING — RUN #2 EXAMINATION REPORT
**Subject:** "The Clockwork Ferry of Oakhaven" — generated by Google AI Studio Build (Gemini 4 Neon, per the build record; generation **10m 03s** per the browser-runner's report — the examiner did not witness the generation and treats the time/model as runner-reported) from Gemini's Run #2 spec: two places from ONE data schema, portals, hash routing, teardown hygiene, offline purity.
**Export examined:** `~/workspace/research_notes/aistudio-exports/clockwork-ferry-source.zip` (154,217 B), extracted unmodified to `living-universe/vibe-experiment-exam/run2/`. The zip was never altered; the one deliberate modification made during this examination (the third-place schema test) was applied to the exam copy only, is documented in §3, and was reverted afterward — the exam tree again matches the zip byte-for-byte in source, and the rebuilt bundle returned to its original size (214.98 kB).
**Method:** full source read · safety grep sweep · plain local install/build/typecheck · static serve of the production build · three puppeteer drivers written for this examination (desktop 1280×800 with full external-network blockade + listener/rAF census + canvas-pixel avatar tracking; a focused slide/wipe driver; mobile 375×812 touch at DSF 2) · a physics simulation run against the app's own compiled `physics.ts` + `places.ts` · the examiner's own visual read of the captured frames (kept in `vibe-experiment-exam/run2/shots/`; raw results in `results-desktop.json`, `results-slide.json`, `results-mobile.json`, `results-schema.json` beside the drivers).
**Examiner's verdict, up front:** Run #2 was commissioned to answer the question Run #1 left open — *can the generator build the reusable engine, not another single room?* On the evidence below: **yes, for the engine's skeleton.** The schema proof (§3) is the decisive result of the night: a third place the generator never saw was instantiated from data and traversed both ways through the unmodified engine. Of the spec's 14 legs: **12 PASS · 1 PARTIAL (sliding — a proven corner wedge) · 1 PASS with a graded blemish (mobile badge truncation)**. Clean install, zero-call, teardown and console legs — three of Run #1's four factory-test failures — all pass outright. **No blanket PASS is issued**: the corner wedge, the badge truncation, and the compile-time asterisk on the schema claim (§3) stand as findings, and §8 grades ChatGPT's demonstration points separately, two of which are absent by this run's design.

## 1 · ARCHITECTURE

**Inventory (4,709 lines total, incl. config and data):**

| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `src/engine/renderer.ts` | 1,962 | Generic canvas painter over the schema (layered: backdrop → water → under-deck props → gears → deck → threshold pads → Y-sorted props/doors/avatar → ceiling lamps → markers → mist/rain → vignette → wipe curtain) |
| `src/world/places.ts` | 737 | **The world as data** — both places, complete: palette, ambient systems, deck polygon, walkable polygon, obstacles, spawns, portals, props, inspectables |
| `src/engine/worldEngine.ts` | 677 | Simulation: avatar state, waypoint + keyboard movement, portal triggers, two-phase transition state machine, ambient particles, hash sync |
| `src/engine/physics.ts` | 338 | Pure math: dt clamp, polygon clamp/constrain, circle-vs-circle/rect push-out, sliding resolver, 2.5-D camera |
| `src/world/schema.ts` | 203 | The type contract: `PlaceDefinition`, `PortalDef`, `ObstacleDef`, `PropDef`, `InspectableDef`, … |
| `src/App.tsx` | 186 | Shell: engine created **once** in a ref, hash subscription with echo guard, badge + drawer mounting |
| `src/components/WorldCanvas.tsx` | 173 | Canvas + the single rAF loop + DPR cap + input |
| `src/engine/audio.ts` | 122 | Zero-asset WebAudio synth (footsteps, doorway tones, chimes) |
| `src/components/InspectionDrawer.tsx` | 107 | Bottom-sheet fixture inspector with stepper |
| `src/components/LocationBadge.tsx` | 89 | Place plaque + Doorway/Fixtures/mute controls |
| `src/engine/hashRouter.ts` | 48 | `#/place/<id>[/inspect/<id>]` parse/build, generic over `PLACES` keys |
| `index.html`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/index.css`, configs | — | Vite 5 + React 18 + TS shell; system font stacks only |

**Build shape:** Vite 5.4.11 + React 18.3.1 + TypeScript (strict `tsc --noEmit` clean) — the spec's pins, exactly. Production bundle **214.98 kB JS (67.84 kB gzip) + 18.56 kB CSS** — a third smaller than Run #1's (290.88/91.0 + 35.21) while doing strictly more.

**How each system is implemented:**
- **Places as data (the headline).** Every fact about both worlds — geometry, palettes, lantern/gear/porthole systems, prose — lives in `places.ts` as JSON-serializable data typed by `schema.ts`. The renderer and engine contain **no per-place branches on place identity for structure** (the only place-id literals outside the data are three cosmetic cases, §3). Contrast Run #1: one room existed only as ~1,800 lines of imperative draw calls.
- **Locomotion.** Desired velocity from WASD/arrows or a click waypoint, with arrival deceleration over the last 34 world units, facing blended toward motion, procedural leg swing from `walkPhase`, idle breathing bob. Movement is resolved by `resolveSlidingMovement` — there is **no waypoint routing** (see §5).
- **Portals as data + a transition state machine.** A portal is `{standPoint, triggerRadius, doorFrame, targetPlaceId, targetSpawnId, transitionDirection}`. Walking within the trigger radius starts `opening` (220 ms eased door swing, avatar steps to the threshold) → `wiping` (400 ms directional curtain; the scene swap commits at progress ≥ 0.5, under the curtain's opaque peak; avatar placed at the *exact* `targetSpawnId`, camera snapped during the swap) → `idle`, with a 0.42 s portal cooldown against bounce-back.
- **Hash routing.** `#/place/<id>` (+ optional `/inspect/<id>`); `App` writes the hash on engine-driven changes, guards its own writes with `lastWrittenHashRef`, and routes external hash changes (Back/Forward/manual) into `syncFromHashRoute`, which finds the connecting portal in the current place to preserve transition direction.
- **Teardown by architecture.** The engine, the rAF loop and every listener are created once for the app's lifetime; a place switch is a state change inside the engine, never a remount (WorldCanvas's effect deps are `[engineRef]`; its cleanup cancels the rAF, disconnects the ResizeObserver and removes all four window listeners). §4 proves the census stays flat.
- **Sound.** Synthesized WebAudio — footsteps (timber vs interior by the place's `environmentKind` data field), doorway latch tones, inspection chimes. Zero audio assets, zero network.

- **Clean-install leg (Stranger Test): PASS — the leg Run #1 failed.** Plain `npm install`, no flags: **81 packages in 55 s, no ERESOLVE.** (Run #1's self-inflicted `esbuild ^0.25` vs `vite ^8` peer conflict is absent; there is no direct esbuild pin.) `npm run build` succeeds; `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- **Zero-call proof: PASS, outright.** Source grep: **zero** `http://`/`https://` references in `src/`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`; no `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, or axios anywhere. Fonts are system stacks (Run #1's Google Fonts call is gone). The built bundle contains only inert URL strings (W3C XML namespace identifiers, React's error-decoder URL in an error path, a Tailwind license comment) — no endpoints. **Runtime proof:** the entire desktop examination ran with request interception aborting every non-localhost request — **zero external attempts were made**; the full request ledger for two pages, 8+ traversals, Back/Forward and the slide test is 13 requests, all `localhost` (page, JS, CSS, and the browser's automatic `favicon.ico`).

## 3 · THE SCHEMA PROOF (decisive test)

**Procedure.** On the exam copy only: (1) added a complete third place, `engine_room` ("The Brasswell Engine Room"), to `places.ts` — own palette, walkable polygon, 3 obstacles, 3 props (existing kinds only), 1 ceiling lantern, 2 gears, 1 inspectable, 1 spawn, 1 return portal; (2) added one portal to `ferry_cabin`'s data (`portal_engine_room`, stand point (690,648), target `engine_room`/`from_ferry_cabin`) and one new spawn to `ferry_cabin` (`from_engine_room`, (640,648)); (3) widened the `PlaceId` union in `schema.ts` by one literal. **No engine, renderer, physics, router, or component code was touched.** Typecheck clean; bundle grew 214.98 → 218.33 kB (+3.35 kB for an entire place).

**Runtime evidence** (`driver-schema.cjs`, `results-schema.json`, shots `s0–s2`):
- Fresh load at `#/place/engine_room` renders the new place (badge "The Brasswell Engine Room", its own palette/gears/lamp, return hatch labeled "Wheelhouse Hatch").
- Clicking the new portal's threshold in the cabin **traverses into the engine room** through the standard opening→wipe→spawn sequence.
- The engine room's own portal returns to the cabin, spawning the avatar at the **new** `from_engine_room` spawn — `s2` shows the avatar standing beside the newly added Engine Room Hatch in the cabin, its door frame, label and threshold pad all rendered as first-class citizens.
- Direct hash navigation `#/place/engine_room` also routes correctly. **Zero errors across the run.**

**Verdict: PASS — with one compile-time asterisk, stated precisely.** At runtime and at the architecture level the claim holds completely: places are data, the engine is place-blind. The asterisk: the *type layer* is part of the data's surface — `PlaceId` is a closed union (`schema.ts:1`), so a type-checked build cannot accept a new place from `places.ts` alone; one line in `schema.ts` must widen. Two further closed vocabularies bound what data can express: `PropKind` (16 kinds; the renderer's `drawProp` switch at `renderer.ts:491` has no default — an unknown kind would render nothing) and `environmentKind` / door-frame style (2 each). A third place can only *recombine the existing visual vocabulary* — visibly so in `s1`, where the reused `cabin_bulkhead_shell` prop draws an empty porthole ring because its drawing presumes the cabin's porthole bank. And two cosmetic engine branches key on place identity: the hash-nav direction fallback (`worldEngine.ts:240`, names `'ferry_cabin'`) and the doorway sound choice (`worldEngine.ts:465`, `targetPlaceId === 'ferry_cabin'`) — a third place inherits the default branch of each; traversal is unaffected. None of this rescues Run #1's position (a second place was *impossible* there); it defines the exact altitude of Run #2's win: **a data-authored world over a fixed visual vocabulary, with the id registry kept in the type system.**

## 4 · TRAVERSAL + TEARDOWN (scripted, production build)

- **Portal traversal, both directions, repeatedly.** Pier→cabin and cabin→pier via the badge's "Walk to Doorway" (which waypoints the portal's stand point; the trigger fires on arrival) plus direct threshold clicks. Hash flips, badge name/subtitle, and spawn all verified each way. **Spawn precision is exact**: the avatar's tracked head sits at screen x 248 on the pier spawn (computed 192 × 1.28 = 246) and at 872 on the return spawn (computed 682 × 1.28 = 873) — placement at `targetSpawnId`, not an approximation.
- **Hash routing — the preview's PARTIAL is settled.** Fresh load from `#/place/ferry_cabin` lands in the cabin. On the **standalone build, Back works** (cabin → pier, badge and hash both revert) **and Forward works** (pier → cabin). The browser-runner's preview failure is therefore the AI Studio preview wrapper's artifact (its iframe history does not deliver Back/Forward to the app), **not an app defect** — the app's `hashchange` subscription (`App.tsx:94`) and `syncFromHashRoute` handle both directions.
- **Teardown census — flat.** Window/document listener nets and live rAF were instrumented from page start and sampled at baseline, after traversal 1, after traversal 2, after six traversals, and at the end: **identical at every checkpoint** — window {resize 1, keydown 1, keyup 1, blur 1, hashchange 1}, document {selectionchange 1}, **rAF live = 1, rAF max = 1** throughout. No leaks; the hygiene is architectural (§1) and the census proves it survives repeated place switches.
- **Clamped dt (Gemini blind spot 1): CLOSED in code.** `MAX_DT_SECONDS = 0.05` (`physics.ts:3`); `clampDeltaTime` (`physics.ts:18`) is applied to every frame's raw dt at the top of `WorldEngine.update`. (At the clamped maximum, one frame's step is 245 × 0.05 = 12.25 world units < avatar radius 20 — tunneling through colliders is arithmetically impossible.)
- **DPR cap (blind spot 2): CLOSED in code and in run.** `Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 2)` (`WorldCanvas.tsx:40`); the mobile session ran at deviceScaleFactor 2 and the canvas backing store measured exactly 750×1624 — the cap, not the hardware, set the size.

## 5 · SLIDING (blind spot 3) — PARTIAL, with a proven corner wedge

**Mechanism.** `resolveSlidingMovement` (`physics.ts:241`) integrates the desired step, then iterates (×4) push-outs against every obstacle and the walkable polygon. Push-out displaces along the contact normal only, so the tangential component survives — on a flat face, that *is* sliding.

**Evidence, two independent kinds.**
1. **Simulation of the app's own physics** (the examiner bundled the shipped `physics.ts` + `places.ts` with esbuild and drove the resolver directly, 60 fps, W+D diagonal from the cabin spawn (298,555) into the chart table, rect x 422–580 · y 416–492): free diagonal until t≈0.67 s at (402, 436.6) — the west face — then **the avatar slides north along the face**: x pinned at ≈402 while y falls 436.6 → 410 over ~0.33 s. Then it **freezes at (402.9, 410) for the remaining 3 s of held input.**
2. **In the running app**, frames `d6` (1.15 s into the same held diagonal) and `d7` (after 2.6 s) show the avatar stationary at the table's west side in both frames — no progress, no jitter, no penetration.

**The wedge, explained.** (402.9, 410) is the table's NW corner trap: the rect corner's push-out (west + north), the walkable polygon's top edge (pushes south, min center y = 410), and the held NE input reach equilibrium. The corridor between the polygon edge (y=390) and the table's top face (y=416) is 26 units — narrower than the avatar's 40-unit diameter — so no valid passage north of the table exists, and a resolver without routing has no way to discover that the way around is *south*. Mouse users are partially protected: click-to-walk cancels a waypoint after 0.28 s without progress (the engine's stuck release), so a click behind the table ends in a clean stop rather than a wedge; a keyboard holder stays wedged until they steer away. No crash, no tunneling — but against the spec's "sliding collision," face-sliding alone is half the behavior: **PARTIAL.**

## 6 · MOBILE 375×812 (touch, DSF 2)

- **No horizontal overflow anywhere**: `documentElement.scrollWidth` = `body.scrollWidth` = `innerWidth` = 375 in both places, before and after walking and traversal.
- **Touch discipline present**: canvas carries `touch-none` + inline `touchAction: 'none'` (`WorldCanvas.tsx`); `overscroll-behavior: none` in `index.css` — the prototype-journey defect Gemini's blind spot 5 named is designed out here.
- **Tap-to-walk works** with camera follow (`m1`: avatar relocated to the tapped deck, view recentered on him).
- **Bottom drawer fits and works**: card rect (12..363 × 477..800) inside the 375×812 viewport; the fixture stepper steps "Fixture 1 / 4" → "Fixture 2 / 4" with the title changing (Harbor Fog Bell → Iron Mooring Bollard); drawer height capped at 42 dvh.
- **Mobile traversal works** (pier→cabin in ~1.9 s including the walk).
- **Blemish — confirmed and quantified (the runner's report was right): the location badge truncates the place name.** The h1's `scrollWidth` is 165 against a `clientWidth` of 140 at 375 px; both places render elided ("Oakhaven Riverba…", "The Brasswell Ferr…", subtitles likewise — visible in `m1`/`m3`). It is a deliberate design choice in `LocationBadge.tsx` (`truncate` inside `max-w-[60vw]`), the badge remains legible as a component and every control fits — but the spec's "location badge" at 375×812 does not show the full place name. Graded as a minor defect on an otherwise passing leg. (The bottom hint pill elides its text the same way.)
- **Zero errors** in the mobile session.

## 7 · CONSOLE — settled

Across all four driver sessions (desktop ×2 pages, slide/wipe, mobile, schema): **zero `pageerror` events and zero application console errors.** The only console entries in any session are three `404` resource logs — the browser's automatic `/favicon.ico` request against the examiner's static file server (the app references no favicon; a local 404, neither an app error nor an external call). What the preview left unverified is settled: **the production build runs error-free.**

## 10 · COMPARISON

**Vs Run #1 (Lantern Archive).** The two runs are bookends: Run #1 proved breadth of *mechanisms in one room*; Run #2 proves the *factory*. Leg by leg: clean install FAIL → **PASS**; zero-call (fonts) FAIL → **PASS clean**; template baggage (unused genai/express/dotenv, phantom server claim) → **absent**; second place impossible → **third place added by the examiner**; doors as in-room furniture → **doors as true place transitions with spawns and hash sync**; mobile modal overflowing 375×667 → **everything fits at 375×812** (badge truncation is a smaller blemish than a clipped Reassemble button); bundle 291 → **215 kB**; generation 10m 04s → 10m 03s (both runner-reported). Run #1 keeps two crowns: its **waypoint routing around the table** (the Ferry has none — §5's wedge is the price) and its **manifestation** (not in this run's brief). The generated line's center of gravity has moved from *drawing a world* to *describing worlds* — which is the direction the house's own architecture took months ago.

**Vs the hand-built engine (house World Engine + Seat E geometry).** The Ferry reads like an independent validation of the house's design decisions, arrived at from a single prompt: schema-first places (our scene schema), normalized coordinates, a clamped master clock (our clock clamp), painter depth from data (our spatial model). Where the two lines diverge is instructive in both directions. The Ferry is *ahead* as an integrated specimen of portal/hash/teardown discipline — its transition contract and its "places are state, not mounts" rule are cleaner than anything our seats have yet wired end-to-end. The house is *ahead* where it deliberately invested: **routing** (geometry.js's `route()` exists precisely so a walker never presses into a corner — the Ferry's wedge is a measured demonstration of why resolution alone is not locomotion), real products and film, verified states, and a world that must survive the Relay, not just a demo. The hand-built prototype journey's verified 375 px behavior also remains the more careful mobile work (no truncated identity).

## 11 · INTEGRATION JUDGMENT (Generator-Neutral: adopt mechanisms, never raw code trust)

**WORTH ADOPTING — re-implemented/verified in our tree:**
1. **The portal/transition contract** — portal as pure data (stand point, trigger radius, door frame, target place + spawn, direction) with the two-phase crossing (220 ms door swing → 400 ms directional wipe, scene swap at the midpoint, camera snap under the curtain, exact spawn). This is the threshold mechanism the World Engine's route graph needs for ChatGPT's point 5, stated completely in one small pattern.
2. **Hash-route sync discipline** — canonical hash construction, the `lastWrittenHash` echo guard, and `syncFromHashRoute`'s trick of finding the *connecting portal* to preserve transition direction on Back/Forward. Our engine routes by hash; this is the cleaner statement of the echo problem.
3. **"Places are state, not mounts" as a named design rule** — one engine, one loop, one listener set for the app's life; swaps as state changes. And its **census as a standing test**: instrumented listener/rAF counts sampled across repeated traversals is a cheap, decisive teardown proof our verification seats can reuse verbatim.
4. **The mobile inspection drawer** — bottom sheet, dvh-capped, fixture stepper with counter; it beat Run #1's modal and our prototype's first mobile pass alike. (Adopt the drawer; reject its badge neighbor — see below.)
5. **Zero-asset WebAudio ambience** — synthesized footsteps/door tones keyed to a place *data* field (`environmentKind`). An offline-honest sound layer for specimens, in the spirit of the house's sound law, at zero asset cost.

**NOT ADOPTED:**
1. **Resolution-only locomotion.** No routing means wedged corners and dead clicks behind furniture. The house keeps geometry.js routing as the standard; the Ferry's corner is now our measured evidence for why.
2. **The "crossfade" name for a curtain wipe.** If the house adopts the transition (item 1 above), it is named honestly — a directional curtain wipe with a midpoint swap — or built as a true dual-render blend. Borrowed vocabulary is how specs rot.
3. **Closed-union place ids as the schema surface.** The house schema keeps ids as open strings with runtime validation (`validateScene`), so "author a place from data alone" is true at *every* layer, not all-but-one.
4. **The truncating badge.** Place identity must never elide on a phone; shrink the type or wrap — the name is the visitor's "you are here."
5. **Place-id cosmetic branches** (`targetPlaceId === 'ferry_cabin'` for sound/direction). Behavior differences belong in place data — the Ferry itself proves the pattern with `environmentKind` and then violates it twice.

**Standing of Run #2:** Gemini's reorder — *thresholds and schema before population and chambers* — is vindicated by measurement. The generated engine's skeleton (schema, portals, router, hygiene, offline purity, clean install) is real, and it converges with the house engine's architecture instead of competing with it: what Vibe Coding manufactured here is not a rival world but a **reference implementation of our own design rules, produced in ten minutes, with its three limits (corner wedge, closed visual vocabulary, flat-illustration rendering) precisely the places where the house's own engineering — routing, data-open schemas, film — already carries the load.** The pipeline verdict from Run #1 stands and strengthens: generate → examine → adopt mechanisms into verified house engines. Run #3 (population) now has a schema worthy of inhabitants.

— Examination seat (Relay), 2026-11-25 night. No deployment made. The captain files this report to the desk.
